hypothesis: The USB0 service loop moves a large response in a few ticks by burst servicing while idle and abandoned hosts cost one pass per tick.
conclusion: Scheduling behavior under the model, not physical throughput.
narrative: checks/usb0-service-burst.py (removed: earlier USB0 service-loop experiments on prior images) ran the actual service loop against a modeled vendor stream, controller and host. With a 20 us host turnaround it moved a 64 KiB response in 13 ticks, a 1,160-byte board frame within one tick and a 2,064-byte request within two ticks. A 256-byte response completed within one tick, and took two ticks if armed-endpoint progress was not counted. A one-pass loop needs one tick per packet: 128 ticks for the 64 KiB response. The model also checked that idle and abandoned hosts cost one pass per tick and that no burst exceeds its budget.

conclusion: The shared descriptors match the replaced copies for the two linked images.
narrative: checks/usb0-service-descriptors.py (removed with the earlier USB0 service-loop experiments) ran the descriptor callbacks of two linked images under Unicorn and compared their bytes; the shared descriptors matched the earlier per-application copies.

hypothesis: Only a vendor request type 0x40 resets the diagnostic channel; standard, class, vendor-interface, vendor-endpoint, reserved and IN request types stall without a reset.
conclusion: Both passed on the host model.
narrative: checks/audit-device-minors-usb-control.py (removed: a one-off audit follow-up needing vendor and object inputs) used the checks/usb-diagnostic-protocol host model to offer the reset request with standard, class, vendor-interface, vendor-endpoint, reserved and IN request types. Each one had to stall without resetting the channel, and request type 0x40 then had to reset it once. checks/usb-zlp.py (removed: waived on a cached build of an earlier DCD image, covered by a733-xhci-*.py and usb-generic-host.py) used Unicorn to verify on the compiled driver that zero-length IN submission arms the transmit register; it resolved that regression and was not a USB controller model.
